bet.text: Design mechanisms that are easy to control, so time goes into scoring instead of arm tuning.

demand.text: The binder ranks no objectives. Its requirements are an arm that scores in any position and picks up from the floor and the single human player station, and an intake that holds cones and cubes while crossing the field and scores them on any node.

auto.text: Autonomous driving uses a simple drive-to-point algorithm on the team's own swerve odometry.
The LEDs flash the alliance color of the auto that is set, in case the wrong one is chosen.
No game piece detection is used.
Odometry is reset to the known spot when the second cone drops, so the third pickup starts without built-up error.

cycle.text: Pick up from the floor or the single human player station. A switch detects a cube; a photo-eye detects a cone and closes the intake. The driver holds the high or mid button, and the chassis drives to a computed scoring pose while the arm moves. Then release and send the arm home.

fallback.text: The operator can home the shoulder and elbow, move both by hand, run and open the intake by hand, and reset the gyro.
The team says the gyro reset was mainly for practice and used once or twice all season in matches.

gave_up.text: The arm does not go all the way around. The team says this did not matter to it, and that an arm pivoting in both directions is harder to counterbalance.

changed.text: The gripper dropped cones at the first event, so gears were added to link its two sides.
A steel bar was added at the rear to lower the center of gravity.
Between the Ontario and world championships, small horns were added because the rollers caught on the swerve modules and ripped.

outcome.text: 61-8-0 in official play; ranked 1 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 83.47, Archimedes).

solves.text: Cross the cable track and charge station and maneuver in the community with traction, agility and stability

facts.text: SDS MK4i L2 modules on Falcon 500s, speed
Frame is 27-3/4 in wide by 31-3/4 in long, in 2 x 1 x 1/8 in aluminum tube
A 1/8 in solid aluminum baseplate keeps the center of gravity low
Odometry accuracy and repeatability improved significantly after adopting Phoenix Pro time sync; a later post calls the gain noticeable but tough to quantify
A driver button locks the wheels at 45 degrees
Tread wear made no noticeable difference to odometry between the two robots; the team says Colson wheels shrink as they wear and can throw odometry off

cost.text: First swerve year: the team put swerve on a wooden chassis and says it took about three months to get it moving

solves.text: Keep debris out of the swerve modules and grease in

facts.text: The covers completely enclose the modules
The top cover came off before and after each event to inspect the modules
The top screws catch about one thread and never came out; a boss with a heat-set insert was planned
Modules are greased with the middle cover on: grease goes in on the end of a zip tie, then the wheels are moved to spread it

solves.text: Give the arm a stable pivot at the right height and angle

facts.text: Lightened 2 x 1 x 1/8 in tube, with a 2 x 2 x 1/8 in rear lower support for rigidity
A 7/8 in dead axle is bolted to the tower with 3/8 in bolts
Fastened with 1/4 in aluminum rivets and bolted to the drivetrain through 1/8 in formed sheet metal

functions.name: Arm

solves.text: Score in any position and pick up from the floor and the single human player station while staying rigid and light

functions.type: two-joint arm, counterbalanced at the shoulder

facts.text: Lightened 2 x 2 x 1/8 in tube; each pivot is three tubes bolted together to carry torque
Pocketed aluminum sprockets are bolted to the arm
Both joints turn on solid dead axles with press fit bronze bushings
Two 50 lb gas shocks counterbalance the shoulder and go over center to hold it in the starting configuration; two magnets hold the elbow
Geometry and design are heavily based on the team's 2011 robot

cost.text: A crack and a slightly deformed tube wall showed at the top pivot of the practice robot, so 1/4 in aluminum plates were added with four #8 bolts

functions.name: Shoulder Gearbox

solves.text: Move the shoulder fast with so little backlash that no external encoder is needed

functions.type: custom gearbox with two chain stages

facts.text: Falcon 500, about 18:1 in the gearbox, then 2:1 in #25 chain and nearly 4:1 in #35 chain; 133:1 overall
Gears are bonded to the shaft with retaining compound, and the final gear has a wide custom broached hub
An idler adds chain wrap on the driving sprocket
The retaining compound is Loctite 609, which fills sloppy hex bores where torque is lower; the wide hub on the final stage bolts to a stock gear

functions.name: Elbow Gearbox

solves.text: Move the elbow fast with so little backlash that no external encoder is needed

functions.type: custom gearbox with one chain stage

facts.text: Falcon 500, about 34:1 in the gearbox, then 4:1 in #25 chain; 138:1 overall
A 1/4 in pocketed aluminum plate with a 3/16 in polycarbonate top plate and a 3D printed cover

solves.text: Pick up cones and cubes quickly from the floor and station, and hold them while crossing the field

facts.text: A pneumatic top roller in carbon fiber and silicone tubing adds grip on cubes and assists the 4 in compliant wheels
Pneumatic side rollers pinch and center cones; a four-bar with two polycarbonate sector gears times the two sides
One Falcon 500 drives the top roller and one drives both side rollers
Almost all pocketed 1/4 in polycarbonate, with side plates bolted into tapped edges
The team looked at the robot the Cheesy Poofs ran in 2019 and built around it
It tolerates side to side misalignment and centers the cone itself; the team credits this, repeatable odometry and automatic alignment for its auto success

cost.text: It dropped cones at the first event, before the two sides were linked by gears
A fan's account says collisions broke the claw in the second of its two division playoff losses, and the robot could not pick up after that

solves.text: Detect that a piece is held and act on it automatically

facts.text: A bumper switch detects a cube and stops the rollers so they do not damage it
A photo-eye detects a cone and closes the intake
There is no color sensor; the driver picks cone or cube, because side roller speeds and top roller position differ by piece

solves.text: Drive to the scoring position while the arm is still moving

facts.text: A Limelight V3 tracks reflective tape for cones and AprilTags for cubes
The robot computes a scoring pose from distance and heading to the target, and drives there while the arm moves
The Limelight sits in the drivetrain, angled up
Limelight target angles give distance and heading to the goal and odometry gives the robot pose; the same function runs in auto and teleop

solves.text: Control the arm with the easiest control scheme available

facts.text: A finite state machine runs arm and gripper; Motion Magic moves both joints to set positions
No position feedforward on either joint; the gas springs make the shoulder weight neutral and also damp it, so gains and acceleration could be fairly aggressive
They signal cone or cube across the field and turn red if the Limelight is not connected
They flash white when a piece is held, for pickups the driver cannot see

functions.name: Autonomous driving

solves.text: Make autos that are repeatable without path following

functions.type: drive-to-position function with slew rate limits

facts.text: The function takes a field position and heading with maximum linear and rotational speeds, and computes the velocities to get there
Autos string points together; an aggressive slew rate limiter on the field-relative velocities makes them look like a smooth path
It moves to the next point once within a tolerance of the last; if that is large enough the robot does not slow down first
Odometry drift is very repeatable, so the commanded positions are adjusted for it instead of correcting from 3D vision poses
For repeatable odometry the team rates wheel alignment, chassis squareness and flatness, wheel offsets and build quality as the biggest factors

decisions.because: they have a lower center of gravity, better stability and known reliability

decisions.choice: Minimal backlash in both arm gearboxes
decisions.because: the motor encoders can then position the joints with no external encoder
designing the whole system to need no elaborate control scheme is often much easier than tuning an advanced one

decisions.choice: Polycarbonate gears linking the two gripper sides
decisions.because: the robot dropped cones at its first event

decisions.choice: Bronze bushings on the arm pivots
decisions.because: their size and weight suit high loads where low friction is not required

decisions.choice: Timing belts on the top roller
decisions.because: they need no tensioning and weigh less

decisions.choice: Side plates bolted into tapped polycarbonate edges
decisions.because: it removes the need for aluminum brackets
the team found the code was not the most accurate
the Limelight is angled up at cone nodes and tags, and the team did not find detection necessary
they are simpler to understand, implement and tune, and more flexible
decisions.instead_of: more elaborate path following or planning

decisions.because: the simpler vision method runs at frame rates high enough to need no latency compensation
